appellations.name: Gaiole
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
Gaiole in Chianti spreads across the eastern Monti del Chianti, a high, wooded commune of castles and abbeys that includes Brolio, Coltibuono, Ama, Cacchiano and Meleto. Soils are galestro and alberese with macigno sandstone on the heights, and altitudes run from about 300 to 650 m, so the wines range from firm and structured in the south to fragrant and lean in the north.

At Brolio, Baron Bettino Ricasoli set out in 1872 the recipe on which Chianti was later based. Castello di Ama, Badia a Coltibuono, Barone Ricasoli, Riecine, Rocca di Montegrossi and San Giusto a Rentennano are leading estates.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 295 to 675 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Ricasoli's 1872 letter recommended Sangiovese for body and aroma, Canaiolo to soften it, and Malvasia for wines meant to be drunk young.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Greve
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
The Greve UGA is the commune of Greve in Chianti minus the three UGAs carved out of it (Panzano, Lamole and Montefioralle). It runs from the Greve valley floor up the slopes of the Monti del Chianti toward the high ridge of Ruffoli, so it spans a wide range of altitudes and soils: alberese and galestro, with sandstone (macigno) on the eastern heights. Greve town, with its funnel-shaped piazza, is the market centre of the northern Chianti.

Querciabella, a biodynamic pioneer in the high Ruffoli area, Castello di Verrazzano (home of the navigator Giovanni da Verrazzano) and Vignamaggio (where Lisa Gherardini, the probable sitter of the Mona Lisa, is said to have lived) are the best-known estates.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 175 to 690 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Castellina
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
Castellina in Chianti, one of the three founding members of the medieval Lega del Chianti with Radda and Gaiole, sits on the ridge that splits the Pesa and Elsa valleys, at the centre of the zone. Its soils are the most varied of Chianti Classico: alberese and galestro in the east, sandstone, and Pliocene sands and clays on the western slopes toward the Elsa. The wines are balanced and fruity, between the ripeness of the south and the tension of Radda.

Castello di Fonterutoli (Mazzei), Castellare di Castellina, Rocca delle Macìe, Nittardi, Tenuta di Lilliano and Cecchi are based here.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 205 to 575 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: The Mazzei family has owned Fonterutoli since 1435; a Mazzei, the notary Ser Lapo, wrote the earliest known document using the name Chianti for wine, in 1398.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: San Casciano
appellations.village: San Casciano in Val di Pesa
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
San Casciano is the northern gateway to Chianti Classico, on the lower, gentler hills of the Val di Pesa toward Florence. Much of the commune lies below 400 m, on marine Pliocene sands and clays with river pebbles, and on alberese limestone and galestro on the higher ground to the south. The climate is the mildest of the zone, and the wines are generous, round and early to charm, with ripe cherry and softer tannin than the high sites of the Monti del Chianti.

Antinori's cellar at Bargino, dug into the hillside, and its Tignanello estate are here, as are the Castelli del Grevepesa cooperative and the villa of Sant'Andrea in Percussina, where Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince in exile.
appellations.terroir: Pliocene sands, clays and pebbles on the lower hills; alberese and galestro to the south. The UGA as a whole lies at about 125 to 375 m (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Marchesi Antinori (Tignanello, Antinori nel Chianti Classico)
appellations.nerd_note: Tignanello was first made in 1970 as a Chianti Classico Riserva, became a table wine with the 1971 vintage and added Cabernet from 1975; it is often named among the first 'Super Tuscans'.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Radda
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
Radda in Chianti was the capital of the medieval Lega del Chianti and is the reference for high-altitude, galestro-driven Sangiovese: vineyards at roughly 350 to 650 m among woods, cool nights and poor, stony soils of galestro, alberese and some sandstone. The wines are pale, perfumed and nervy, sometimes austere in youth, with red fruit, orange peel and a long, saline line; warmer summers have made Radda one of the most sought-after names of the 2010s.

Montevertine, whose Le Pergole Torte (1977) was one of the first pure-Sangiovese Super Tuscans, Castello di Volpaia, Monteraponi, Val delle Corti, Istine and Caparsa are references.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 350 to 725 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Vagliagli
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary: A UGA in the western part of Castelnuovo Berardenga around the hamlet of Vagliagli, higher and cooler than the southern part of the commune, at roughly 250 to 470 m. Alberese limestone and sandstone give Sangiovese with more tension and perfume than the warm Berardenga, and the area is a patchwork of woods and vines. Dievole, Fattoria della Aiola and Bindi Sergardi are among its estates.
appellations.terroir: Alberese limestone and sandstone, with woods covering much of the land. The UGA as a whole lies at about 255 to 465 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: San Donato in Poggio
match: Chianti Classico San Donato in Poggio
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
This UGA joins the Chianti Classico part of Barberino Tavarnelle with the northern tip of Poggibonsi, centred on the walled village of San Donato in Poggio on the ridge between the Pesa and Elsa valleys. Alberese and galestro on the ridge, and sands and clays on the western slopes, give firm, medium-bodied Sangiovese.

Isole e Olena, whose Cepparello became a benchmark pure Sangiovese, Castello di Monsanto, whose Il Poggio (1962) is often cited as the first single-vineyard Chianti Classico, and Antinori's Badia a Passignano are here.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 210 to 450 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Castelnuovo Berardenga
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
The southernmost and warmest UGA, where Chianti Classico runs down toward the clay hills of the Crete Senesi east of Siena. More clay, marine Pliocene sands and alberese, a lower average altitude and a warmer, drier climate give the ripest, fullest and most generous Sangiovese of the zone, dark-fruited and broad.

Fèlsina, which has labelled its wines 'Berardenga' for decades and whose Rancia is a reference single-vineyard Chianti Classico, Castell'in Villa, San Felice and Fattoria di Petroio are here.
appellations.terroir: The UGA as a whole lies at about 235 to 565 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Panzano
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
Panzano is the frazione in the south-west of Greve commune famous for the Conca d'Oro, the 'golden shell', a south-facing amphitheatre below the village on galestro and alberese that collects heat and gives some of the most complete Sangiovese in Tuscany: dark cherry, violets and a firm, mineral frame.

Fontodi, the Manetti family estate whose Flaccianello della Pieve is a reference for pure Sangiovese, Castello dei Rampolla, Il Molino di Grace, La Massa, Le Cinciole and Vecchie Terre di Montefili are here. Panzano's growers formed one of Italy's first organic districts, and most of the vineyard is farmed organically.
appellations.terroir: Galestro (friable schistous clay) and alberese limestone; the Conca d'Oro faces south below Panzano village. The UGA as a whole lies at about 275 to 655 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Giovanni Manetti of Fontodi has chaired the Consorzio Vino Chianti Classico, which pushed the UGA project.
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Montefioralle
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary: A small UGA around the walled medieval village of Montefioralle on the hill just west of Greve, believed to be the family home of the Vespucci (of Amerigo Vespucci). Its slopes of alberese and galestro rise to about 500 m between the Greve and Pesa valleys and give fragrant, mid-weight Sangiovese with good acidity. With Vagliagli it is one of the two UGAs without a long history as a named wine area.
appellations.terroir: Alberese limestone and galestro on the ridge west of Greve. The UGA as a whole lies at about 230 to 505 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Lamole
appellations.grapes: Sangiovese (at least 90% for Gran Selezione)
appellations.summary:
The smallest and highest UGA, a hamlet of terraces high above Greve, with vineyards at roughly 450 to 650 m and the UGA as a whole reaching about 850 m. Dry-stone walls, many rebuilt by hand since the 1990s, hold the slopes, and the soils are sandstone (macigno), poor and acid-leaning, unlike the limestone of most of Chianti Classico.

The result is pale, high-toned, floral Sangiovese with bright acidity and fine tannin, closer to a mountain wine; the old bush-trained vines (*alberello*) on the terraces are a rarity in Tuscany. Castello di Lamole, Lamole di Lamole, I Fabbri and Castellinuzza e Piuca are the main producers.
appellations.terroir: Macigno sandstone terraces, among the highest vineyards of Chianti Classico. The UGA as a whole lies at about 430 to 855 m (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: UGA (unità geografica aggiuntiva) of Chianti Classico DOCG, one of 11 voted by producers in June 2021 and approved by the Ministry in 2023 (DM 22 June 2023). The UGA name may appear on Gran Selezione labels; the Consorzio intends to extend it to Annata and Riserva.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Montmains
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Montmains is one of the great left-bank premiers crus of Chablis, a long slope south-west of the town facing south-east, on thin, stony Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. This polygon is the lieu-dit itself (Les Monts-Mains in the land register); the principal name also covers Forêts and Butteaux, which may be sold as Montmains or under their own names. The wines are taut, saline and mineral, with less flesh than the right bank but great precision.
appellations.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 170 to 210 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Chablis premier cru: one of the 17 principal climats of the cahier des charges, which can also cover satellite climats.

appellations.name: Chablis premier cru Butteaux
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A satellite climat of Montmains, higher up the left-bank slope and facing south-east, drawn here from the lieux-dits Le Bout and Le Milieu des Buttaux. Raveneau's Butteaux, from old vines, is one of the most admired left-bank Chablis: lean and stony when young, deep and long with age.
appellations.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 220 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Montmains, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

Its satellites Troesmes and Côte de Savant may be sold under the Beauroy name. The wines are fresh, floral and quite delicate, often good value among the premiers crus.

appellations.name: Comtats de Barcelona
appellations.grapes: Macabeo, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay; Trepat, Garnacha, Monastrell and Pinot Noir for rosé
appellations.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
appellations.summary:
Comtats de Barcelona ('the counties of Barcelona') is the Catalan heart of Cava, covering the great majority of production, with the town of Sant Sadurní d'Anoia in the Penedès as its capital. Its five subzones are Valls d'Anoia-Foix, Serra de Mar, Conca del Gaià, Serra de Prades and Pla de Ponent. Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada are the classic trio, Xarel·lo giving body and longevity.

Codorníu, which made Spain's first traditional-method sparkling wine in 1872, and Freixenet are based in Sant Sadurní, as are Juvé & Camps and Recaredo. Some of the best growers have left the DO: Raventós i Blanc in 2012 to create Conca del Riu Anoia, and Gramona, Recaredo and others in 2019 to form Corpinnat.
appellations.terroir: Limestone, clay and sandy soils from the Mediterranean coast to the inland plateau.

appellations.name: Rioja Oriental
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
appellations.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
appellations.summary:
Rioja Oriental, called Rioja Baja until 2018, is the eastern zone: 49 municipalities of La Rioja and Navarra downstream from Logroño to Alfaro, plus the valleys of the Leza, Jubera, Cidacos and Alhama. The climate is the warmest and driest of the region, with a strong Mediterranean influence, and much of the land is low alluvial plain, though vineyards also climb to 600 to 700 m on the slopes of the Sierra de Yerga and the Cidacos valley.

Garnacha was the traditional grape here and still gives some of the zone's most distinctive wines, from old vines on the Yerga; Tempranillo now dominates. The renaming in 2018 was meant to shed the idea that 'Baja' meant lower quality, and estates such as Palacios Remondo in Alfaro have shown what its Garnacha can do.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial plains and terraces along the Ebro, clay and limestone on the slopes; warm, dry Mediterranean climate.

appellations.name: Rioja Alta
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
appellations.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
appellations.summary:
Rioja Alta is the western and highest of Rioja's three zones: 76 municipalities of La Rioja (plus the Burgos enclave of El Ternero) on the south bank of the Ebro from Haro to Logroño and up the valleys of the Tirón, Oja, Najerilla and Iregua, with most vineyards between about 450 and 700 m. The climate has the strongest Atlantic influence in the region: cooler, wetter and later-ripening, so Tempranillo keeps acidity and the wines are built for long ageing.

Soils are clay-limestone, ferrous red clays and stony alluvial terraces along the rivers. Haro's Barrio de la Estación, where López de Heredia, CVNE, La Rioja Alta, Muga, Bilbaínas and Roda stand side by side, is the symbol of classic Rioja, and the zone's long-aged Reservas and Gran Reservas defined the region's style in the twentieth century. Labels may name the zona only when all the grapes come from it.
appellations.terroir: Clay-limestone, ferrous clay and alluvial terraces; Atlantic-influenced climate, the coolest of the three zones.

appellations.name: Levante
appellations.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
appellations.summary: The Levante zone is Requena, on the high plateau west of Valencia at about 600 to 900 m, a continental climate with cold nights that keep acidity in Macabeo and Chardonnay. Requena is the second-largest Cava area after Catalonia; Dominio de la Vega, Pago de Tharsys and Hispano-Suizas are among its producers.
appellations.terroir: High continental plateau of Requena with limestone and clay soils.

appellations.name: Valle del Ebro
appellations.classification: Zona of DO Cava (zoning approved 2020, on labels from 2022): one of four zones, which can appear on labels of Cava de Guarda Superior and above.
appellations.summary: The Valle del Ebro zone gathers the Cava municipalities of La Rioja, Álava, Navarra and Aragón (Zaragoza and Huesca) along the Ebro valley, with two subzones, Alto Ebro and Valle del Cierzo, the latter named after the cold north-west wind of Aragón. Macabeo (Viura) is the main grape, and several Rioja houses make Cava, among them Muga, whose Conde de Haro is one of the best known.

appellations.name: Rioja Alavesa
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo, Viura and others
appellations.classification: Zona of DOCa Rioja: one of three zones that may appear on labels (rules of 2017, labels from 2018), for wines made entirely from grapes of that zone.
appellations.summary:
Rioja Alavesa is the smallest zone: 15 municipalities of the Basque province of Álava on the north bank of the Ebro, on terraces and slopes that climb from the river toward the limestone wall of the Sierra de Cantabria. The sierra shelters the vineyards from cold northern winds, and the soils are pale, chalky clay-limestone, giving Tempranillo of fine acidity, perfume and finesse.

Alavesa has two traditions: the young, carbonic-maceration *vino de cosechero* of small family growers, and the estate wines that made its name, from Marqués de Riscal in Elciego (1858) to Remírez de Ganuza, Remelluri and Ysios. Its growers have pushed hardest for village and single-vineyard labelling, and almost half of Rioja's viñedos singulares are in Álava.
appellations.terroir: Chalky clay-limestone on terraces below the Sierra de Cantabria; vineyards from about 400 m to over 700 m.

appellations.summary: Alfaro is a municipality of Rioja Oriental in La Rioja, at the eastern tip of the DOCa, between the Ebro and the Sierra de Yerga. Its land spans roughly 270 to 750 m. Rioja Oriental is warmer and drier, with Garnacha as the traditional grape and Tempranillo now dominant. The collegiate church of San Miguel carries one of Europe's largest colonies of white storks on a single building. Palacios Remondo, the family estate run by Álvaro Palacios since 2000, showed the potential of the high, cool Garnacha vineyards of the Sierra de Yerga. Recognised viñedos singulares include El Sueño de Amado, Planas Altas, Quiñón de Valmira, Lar de Sotomayor, Domeco de Jarauta, Laderas de Tambarría and Queirón Las Engalladas.

appellations.summary: A small, isolated Cava zone around Almendralejo in Extremadura, in the province of Badajoz, on the flat Tierra de Barros plain at about 300 m. Macabeo and Parellada dominate; Bodegas Vía de la Plata is the best-known producer, and the zone shows how Cava's rules follow a production method rather than a single region.
appellations.terroir: Flat, red clay plain of the Tierra de Barros.

appellations.summary: Laguardia is a municipality of Rioja Alavesa in Álava, the walled medieval capital of Rioja Alavesa, on a hill between the sierra and the Ebro. Founded as a Navarrese frontier town in 1164, it sits on more than 300 old cellars and tunnels; the fabulist Félix María de Samaniego was born here. Ysios, in Santiago Calatrava's wave-roofed winery, and CVNE's Viña Real are here. Its Barrio de la Estación grew up around the station of the Tudela to Bilbao railway (1863), where wineries gathered as French merchants came looking for wine during phylloxera: R. López de Heredia (1877), CVNE (1879), La Rioja Alta (1890), Bodegas Bilbaínas, Gómez Cruzado, Muga and Roda are neighbours. On 29 June the town drenches itself in red wine at the Batalla del Vino. appellations.summary:
Gratallops is where modern Priorat began. In 1989 René Barbier, Álvaro Palacios, Carles Pastrana, Josep Lluís Pérez and Daphne Glorian pooled their grapes in the village to make the first 'Clos' wines, and within a decade Clos Mogador, Clos Erasmus, Clos de l'Obac and Palacios's L'Ermita and Finca Dofí had made Priorat world-famous. The village sits on a ridge above the Siurana river, surrounded by steep terraces of *llicorella*, the dark, crumbling slate that forces vines to root deep and gives the wines their mineral grip.

Old Garnatxa and Carinyena, often blended with Syrah and Cabernet in the early years, give dense, warm wines with a stony, graphite edge.
appellations.terroir: Steep llicorella (slate) terraces above the Siurana. The mapped village area lies at about 150 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 29% (Copernicus DEM).
appellations.nerd_note: Álvaro Palacios's L'Ermita, from a steep slope of old Garnatxa, is one of Spain's most expensive wines.
